relationships.scope: The January 2020 circular asks field offices to use the Issue Tracker under the guideline of 20 August 2018 (it cites the date as 20/08/2019); it adds how issues relate to CPGRAMS and RTI and does not replace the guideline.

effective_date_evidence.quote: The existing “Issue Tracker Portal” is discontinued

evidence.quote: The existing “Issue Tracker Portal” is discontinued

relationships.scope: The July 2026 circular deploys the Samadhan Setu web application for reporting technical issues to the IS Division and states the Issue Tracker portal is discontinued. It replaces the process of the 2018 circular (and the 2020 circular that relies on it); stated in the present tense on the issue date.

limitations: This collection covers Information Services circulars on issue reporting, authentication and cyber security. Network bandwidth orders, pending-issue lists and hardware specifications (see IT hardware specifications and norms) are not included.
The Cyber Security Advisories of 2022 (Nos. 2022/01 to 2022/03 and the e-Office classified-documents advisory) are time-bound alerts; they are listed as circulars but are not standing rules.

The 2020 and 2021 circulars make two-factor and multi-factor authentication mandatory for @epfindia.gov.in e-mail on NIC's direction; only the 17 December 2021 circular states 'with immediate effect', which is recorded. The 2024 circular runs the client-based and web-based VPN together until 15 November 2024 and then disables the client-based VPN; no separate commencement date is recorded.

J-Track (2012) was an earlier issue-reporting arrangement; no circular here says it was replaced by the Issue Tracker. The 2018 circular is cited by the 2020 circular with a different year (2019), which is recorded as written.
The Government of India e-mail policy and IT-resources policy (2015) are forwarded policies; the originals are not reproduced.
Dates follow the letter, not the issuer listing; entries whose letter date differs carry a date_note.

PDFs were read from the issuer mirror on 4 November 2026 because the public site returned 404 for these paths; recorded SHA-256 values apply to those files. Scanned pages are OCR. Issue dates were checked against the document headers.
